newsitem.title: USA: Knowles signs bills on city funding, sport fees.
newsitem.headline: Knowles signs bills on city funding, sport fees.

text.p: Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles on Thursday signed bills that revamp distribution of state funds to municipalities and increase sport-fishing fees charged to tourists.
The so-called "Safe Communities Bill" replaces traditional municipal revenue sharing with state funding dispersed to municipalities for law enforcement and health protection.
It was unanimously endorsed by members of the Alaska Conference of Mayors and Alaska Municipal League.
The bill provides for a minimum $40,000 entitlement to all communities, up from the previous minimum of $25,000.

Knowles, a Democrat, said he believes the Republican-controlled legislature's recent six percent cut to state funding for municipalities was too sharp. But the new bill will mitigate some of the effects, especially for the tiniest communities, he said.
The mayor of Alaska's largest city said the new formula benefits towns of various populations.
"It's good for the people of Anchorage and, I believe, all the people of Alaska," said Anchorage Mayor Rick Mystrom, a Republican.
The other bill signed by Knowles increases fees charged to visitors for sport fishing, hunting and trapping licenses but slightly decreases fees charged to Alaska residents.
Under the bill, 14-day non-resident sport fishing licenses will cost $50 each, up from $30; annual non-resident soprt fishing licenses will cot $100 each, up from $50.
Those increases are unlikely to discourage tourists from fishing in Alaska, Knowles said.
"Frankly, I think few non-resident anglers will blink at the increase because they know Alaska has the best fishing in North America," he said.
Overall, the bill is expected to produce net new revenues of $4.5 million for the state, Knowles said.
